errors.what: The DIVERGING verdict was computed from the per-TOKEN loss curve, which rises mechanically as minted tokens get longer, while a unit-stable bits/byte curve sat in the same report unused.
Banner lie again: the [config] PATH line still described the transition matrix after CHAIN_ROUTE=soc became the default.
LR_WARMUP=1000 exceeded a toy run's 360 total steps, so the run never left warmup and trained at a third of peak throughout — looked like the schedule hurting.

Stale checkout: a pilot ran at commit 99ba0f400f, three commits behind, and produced a result byte-identical to the two before it (held-out 2.893). Three runs of the same config, ~1 hour of GH200 time, nothing new.
The report's verdict contradicted its own cross-check — printed DIVERGING on a run whose bits/byte curve was flat (-0.007) over the last two thirds, because it measured from the global minimum.
longrun.sh seeds display bug: seq newlines broke the banner echo of the seed list.

`fab.note_dom(int(_w[0].argmax()), did)` recorded ONE expert (row 0, argmax) per step; at BATCH_W=16 that is 15 of 16 windows never recorded — hence 'serving none: 4053'. Consequences: dom_ban (the breadth cap the researcher asked for) was effectively inert, and society()'s `use` table was sampled at 1/16 the rate of chaining's, so every ROUTER SELECTION comparison across paths (516 vs 202 vs 877 experts, top 3.7% vs 5.1% vs 25.2%) compared unlike things.

generate() samples the LIVE model at end of training and there was no best-checkpoint tracking anywhere; ckpt.pt is written on a cadence and overwritten. Every text sample in the project came from a model ~41,000 steps past its best, 1.1–1.3 b/B worse.
The best-checkpoint block was inserted inside the `except` handler, so it only ran when the curve sample failed.

_VALT/_BL cached the tokenised held-out text once and were never invalidated at re-tokenisation, so from the first mint the mid-run learning curve scored the model against validation text in an obsolete segmentation. Invalidated the '+1.220 bits/byte since its own minimum' and the 'memory masks weight degradation' claim.
A bad string-replace appended an orphan `return True` at module scope → IndentationError at line 2966/2968; two verification runs came back rc=1.
_save_ckpt returned early on SAVE_CKPT=0 without signalling, and the caller assumed success — a real log printed 'saved to None.best' on a run that saved nothing.
TOK_COMPOSE first version sized the composed table to the LIVE vocab, which can lag the stream → IndexError: index 331 out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 300, killing the arm.
A duplicate `import os` was inserted into tokenizer.py by the edit script.

pilot_gru_8 ran TOK_COMPOSE=1 and TOK_MINT_NOVEL=0.5 simultaneously (Claude made the composer default-on then recommended novelty minting on top), so the worst result in the project attributes to neither change.

_total_steps = EPOCHS × (tokens // WIN) measured ONCE at the seed vocabulary. Minted tokens are longer, so later epochs are shorter — pilot_gru_8 projected 81,840 steps and ended at ~48,800, a 40% overestimate. It fed the ETA, the kB/s and GB/day figures, the 'SAMPLED FROM step ~N' label, and the cosine LR horizon.
Workflow tool call rejected: 'InputValidationError: An unexpected parameter run_in_background was provided'.
The bisect workflow's returned JSON did not have the expected keys (FLAGGED: [], SURVIVING: [], SCREENED CLEAN: None); the real per-agent verdicts had to be dug out of journal.jsonl.

User-side run failures: repeat run3 died at step 8800 (log ends mid-training); run2 hit 'cusolver error: CUSOLVER_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR' and skipped the SIGNATURE SPACE diagnostic; a terminal was closed mid-run leaving a .partial1 log.

fab_logits fabricates `gist = torch.zeros(...)` on eval paths; Fabric.forward then calls ground_update on it, and F.normalize(zeros) is zeros, so every eval forward dragged the top-8 experts' region centroids TOWARD THE ORIGIN, five times per call (entry + 4 hops). Present in every run the project has ever done via the RATE_EVERY learning-curve sample, and extra under SAVE_CKPT, so pilot/grid and seeds/repeat were never comparable.

Structural gap after a mint: GROW_EVERY=100 vs RETOK_EVERY=3000 means a newly minted token cannot appear as input or target for up to 3000 steps, yet sits in the softmax denominator warm-started to a HIGH logit — a strict loss increase by construction. pilot_gru_8 logged +317 tokens waiting at once (~15% of the vocabulary).

EPOCHS silently rewrites the cosine LR horizon, so four runs compared as 'same config, different length' were four different optimization schedules; and because the frozen-vocab run's step projection is exact, freezing the vocabulary accidentally fixed the LR schedule — perfectly confounding the tokenizer result.

Harness arm-flag precedence: `env $FLAGS ... VMAX=2048 ...` puts hardcoded values AFTER the arm flags, and the last assignment wins, so arm flags for VMAX, WIN, BATCH_W, RATE_EVERY, CKPT_EVERY, GROW_EVERY/BURST, SEG_MIN/MAX, DATA_DIR, LAYERS, MODEL were silently discarded — while the log was still named after the value that never took effect. Affects grid, seeds and repeat, so past grid arms may not have run what their names claim.

`seeds` and `repeat` never got the fetch-if-empty corpus guard that `pilot` and `grid` carried, so they parsed args, made their output dir, printed a banner and died inside the model on 'no corpus files in data_pilot/train/eng/'.

GEN_PROCS=4 caps how many DOMAINS get a continuation; with one corpus that is exactly ONE 200-token sample, and the composing check scored '% of generated words in the training text' on 64–91 words. Every text judgement quoted in the project (91%/71%/31%) rests on that.

data/dyntok.json is written unconditionally by every online run (line 4117). With TOK_ONLINE=0 it IS loaded, so a run inherits whatever vocabulary the previous run left behind — making seeds non-independent and results order-dependent for the frozvocab arm and any past grid arm using it.

With TOK_MINT_UNTIL set, 39 no-op retokenizations still fired (every 3000 steps), each printing the banner lie 'minting live', clearing _VALT/_BL and _sigq pointlessly, and calling fabgrow.note_shift(step) — which blacked out fabric growth for FAB_COOLDOWN=400 of every 3000 steps, ~13% of the run.

The isolation script meant to prove the new composite-lever layer changes nothing failed with a SyntaxError while stripping torch imports ('levers, line 19: , torch.nn as nn, torch.nn.functional as F'). Retry in flight at the chunk boundary.
No gradient clipping anywhere in the training loop — no clip_grad_norm_ at LR=2e-3 on AdamW with a GRU, a population growing to 4096 experts, and a vocabulary changing underneath it.

notes:
Scope note: entries labelled `USER` that contain only a `[RESULT]` block are tool output, not the human; I excluded those and used only genuine human turns for `ideas`. A context-compaction summary written by Claude appears inline at 2026-08-06T14:14:36 (lines 3691–3838) and restates earlier user messages verbatim — I did NOT treat those restatements as new researcher input, only the live USER turns in this chunk's timespan.

Standing constraints restated in that summary and still in force: work on branch `rm-predict`; never overwrite anything under `runs/`; confirm before action on performance changes; no compromises (do not remove functionality for speed); do not run the smoke gate locally.

The arc of this chunk in one line: a sequence of confidently-stated causes for the same phenomenon (tokenizer minting → no LR schedule → seed variance → stale held-out cache → TOK_COMPOSE → commit 18fdd6c → commit 99e5da0 → SAVE_CKPT/zero-gist centroid corruption → the EPOCHS-driven LR horizon), almost every one of which was withdrawn, and in five separate cases withdrawn because the researcher objected first. The researcher's objections have a notably better hit rate than Claude's hypotheses: 'I don't think it is it' (minting), 'we are overoptimizing for the spike', 'it looks more like it broke something', 'we only shut off part of it', and 'I don't think it's because longer epoch' were all borne out. Claude acknowledged this explicitly twice ('Second time your instinct has beaten my read').

Two claims that survived everything in this chunk and are worth carrying forward: (1) runs are bit-for-bit deterministic given (config, commit, SEED) — three identical repeats, md5-verified; (2) TOKENIZER=0 (raw bytes) loses to an order-1 bigram table by 0.538 b/B at 2.6× the steps, so the tokenizer buys most of the model's advantage. Everything else about the tokenizer axis was still open at the chunk boundary.

Best result in the chunk: TOK_MINT_UNTIL=1 (vocab frozen at 512) at EPOCHS=14 — held-out 2.075, beats order-1 by 1.45, 118,743 steps, first non-zero HALT mass (0.4048) ever recorded on a chaining path, gradient reach 23.8%, retention drift -0.069, 92% real words. Caveat the researcher raised and Claude accepted: it is also the longest run and its LR schedule was the only one in the project that annealed correctly, so the cause is not isolated.

Never resolved: the fabric has still not been shown to beat FABRIC=0 on text; coherence remains INCOHERENT (0.08 ± 0.04 against a 0.50 real-text ceiling); and the routing diagnostics (specialization, HALT, H(hop1|hop0)) have repeatedly moved in the opposite direction from text quality.
